[ota-hal] OTA-1740 — nothing wakes a screen that is not about it (LAG-2-5E91)

The second half of Fable's 91C4B8 findings: the React/Zustand cost AROUND a
player action, where LAG-1 took the cost inside one. Five repairs. No gameplay,
combat, movement, economy, vendor-pricing, persistence-cadence, crash-breadcrumb
or deliberate-pacing change, and no world state duplicated.

1. THE 6-SECOND WORLD HEARTBEAT STOPS RE-RENDERING SCREENS IT DOES NOT FEED
   `worldRealtimeTick` runs every ~6 real seconds whatever screen is open and
   replaces the `worldMemory` object several times per beat (patrols, tides,
   faction relations, the war feed, the raid ledger). Exploration, Vendor,
   Contracts, Character — and GiftModal, which Exploration mounts on every
   render — all subscribed to that OBJECT, so four screens re-rendered on a
   wall-clock timer while the player sat still.
   - Each now subscribes to the fields it actually reads. None of Exploration's
     three (visitedRooms / pendingDogOnboarding / enemyIntel) or Contracts'
     eight is realtime, so the heartbeat cannot reach them at all.
   - Where a field IS realtime and IS consumed, the subscription is the DERIVED
     VALUE the screen draws rather than the raw array: the counter takes the
     war-heat number and the tide PRICE MULTIPLIER, not the patrol list; the
     character sheet takes the stepped tide LABEL, not the momentum. So a
     skirmish that does not move a price or turn a fortune does not redraw.
   - Three engine helpers that took a whole `WorldMemory` to read one field
     (getRelation, knownPeople) now declare the Pick they use, which is what
     lets a screen hold the narrow subscription.
   - WorldScreen keeps its whole-memory subscription: it is the live war board
     the heartbeat exists for.
   idle, 5 ticks, 258 items:  Exploration 5 commits/222ms → 0/0
                              Contracts   5/24ms → 0/0
                              Vendor      5/952ms → 4/515ms (real price moves)
                              Character   5/158ms → 5/133ms (displayed tide label)
   a heartbeat that moves only fields nobody reads: all five screens 5 → 0.

2. ONE ACTION'S LOG LINES ARE ONE SUBSCRIBER SWEEP, NOT ONE EACH
   Every `appendLog` was its own zustand set, and a movement step makes many —
   each one a full sweep of every mounted selector (Exploration holds ~57).
   `state/storeNotify.ts` is a store middleware that lets an ordinary GAME-LOG
   write ride along with the next notification the action was going to perform
   anyway, or with a microtask at the end of the turn.
   - ⚠ THE STATE STAYS SYNCHRONOUS. Roughly thirty call sites read `get().gameLog`
     in the same turn they wrote to it — the "have I already said this line"
     guards, the arbiter dedup inside appendLog itself, the talk transcript
     window. A staged log would have broken every one; only the NOTIFICATION is
     deferred.
   - ⚠ NOTHING IS SUPPRESSED. An ordinary gameplay set publishes itself AND the
     log lines held behind it, in order, so a subscriber sees every state change
     it saw before — it just stops being woken once per line of text.
   - TTSController's cold-boot restore check counted arrivals ("2+ entries in one
     tick means a save load"), resting on the one-entry-per-set assumption. It
     now tests the AGE of the arriving log, which is the honest signal and always
     was: a restored log was written in a previous run.
   movement step  21 sweeps in the sync turn → 10   (22 → 11 settled)
   attack round   10 → 5                            (27 → 16 settled)
   five rapid steps  45 → 26      six log lines in one turn  6 → 1

3. THE COUNTER STOPS RE-PRICING THE PACK FOR THINGS THAT CANNOT MOVE A PRICE
   VendorScreen had no memo at all: `reinforceQuote` per weapon, `sellPriceFor`
   twice per sellable row and the recipe menu were rebuilt on every render.
   They are now memos keyed on the inventory array, the vendor, the rapport /
   standing modifier, the war multiplier and the sort — every input that can
   move a price or an eligibility and nothing wider, so a projection can never
   outlive its authority. The hooks sit above the `!player || !vendor` return,
   per OTA-022's rule that every hook precede it.
   the projection work alone, 258 items: 16.6ms per render, now skipped on any
   re-render that could not have moved a price. Vendor mount 1366ms → 909ms.

4. THE ORDINARY TAP LEDGER IS OFF THE GAME STORE
   `logUiTap` ran `appendLog` before every handler in the game, so recording a
   line of diagnostic text swept every mounted subscriber BEFORE the gameplay the
   player asked for began — and `debug` is a HIDDEN channel, so no surface ever
   drew it. It now writes through `persistEntry`, the exact sink appendLog
   persists through, in the same format: COPY LOG and the LogScreen read
   `readFullLog` and are unchanged. `stampLiveBreadcrumb` is untouched and still
   stamped before the handler runs — the crash evidence the OTA/process-death
   investigation reads is exactly as immediate as it was.
   one ordinary tap: 1 store notification before the handler → 0.

5. THE PACK SCALES
   `ItemRow` is memoized and takes two stable handlers (the row's item is passed
   TO them) instead of a fresh closure per row per render, and the whole search →
   fill-mode filter → FUSABLE filter → sort → group pipeline is one memo above
   the guard instead of five passes over a 250-item array on every render.
   ⚠ VIRTUALIZATION WAS EVALUATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FORCED — the reasoning is
   written over the section list: sections open collapsed so the eager list is
   already bounded; the scroll-to-item jump the task requires preserving is built
   on the per-row `onLayout` offsets a virtualized list never records; and under
   react-test-renderer a VirtualizedList would render `initialNumToRender` rows
   and blind every existing inventory suite.
   Inventory mount, 258 items: 316ms → 90ms.  Opening all 16 categories: 61 → 8ms.

Tests: __tests__/ota1740NothingWakesAScreenThatIsNotAboutIt.test.tsx (18 tests)
covers all five — the inert-heartbeat invariant on all five screens, that a
consumed world change still redraws, the one-sweep-per-turn claim with its order
and its synchronous readability, that a gameplay set still notifies and carries
the lines behind it, vendor freshness across inventory / TC / sale / vendor swap,
that a tap notifies nobody while the breadcrumb and the disk line survive, and
that 50 / 100 / 258 rows render, act and absorb a mutation. ota1485, ota1695 and
ota1700 now read the tap ledger from the disk log — same claim, the ledger moved
house; ota1097 and ota1100 pin the row handlers in their useCallback form.
